text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

With the surprising support of Independent Senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston, secured through a A$350 million rural telecommunications and environment package, the A$8 billion partial privatisation of Telstra has been supported by the Senate. Formal Senate endorsement is expected by next week, with the privatisation to commence next year. Page 1.

Australian stockbrokers are enthusiastic about the partial float of Telstra and expect few problems with absorbing the extra A$8 billion in new equity. With a projected market capitalisation of A$35 billion, the float will be a huge boost to the Australian stockmarket. Page 1.

The ACTU is focusing on 'non-discriminatory' wage policies in its presentation to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission. Seeking to block the use of pay rises by employees to "buy" workers out of unions, the ACTU is proposing the intervention of a single member of the AIRC when employees are unfairly discriminating against groups of workers. Page 2.

In response to pressure placed by Independent Senator Brian Harradine, and the Tasmanian Government, the Federal Government has added another A$100 million to its A$1 billion natural heritage trust fund. The extra A$100 million is understood to be targeted almost exclusively at Tasmania, although the Government refused to say. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In what is being described as a political coup for the Federal Government, the A$8 billion one-third sale of Telstra was given the go-ahead yesterday following vital support from two Independent Senators. Legislation to confirm the sale is expected to be assed by the Senate next week after the Howard Government provided concessions totalling A$350 million to Senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston. Page 1.

As the republican debate returns to the agenda, the International Olympic Committee has signalled that it has no objections to the Prime Minister of the day, rather than the Governor-General or the Queen, opening the Sydney 2000 Olympics. Government negotations with the IOC about who should open the games will see the Olympic body allowing Australia to avoid the impending political problem. Page 1.

With the A$8 billion partial-sale of Telstra winning key Senate support, the main beneficiaries of the sale will be Tasmania and Queensland, the home States of the two Independent Senators holding the balance of power. As part of the sale, the Government will spend A$250 million to ensure rural and regional areas have greater telecommunications access and a further A$100 million will be added to the A$1 billion environment fund, with Tasmania to be given preferential treatment for funding allocation. Page 3.

The Federal Government has announced measures which will see airlines and safety authorities dramatically expand information available to consumers on aviation safety records of carriers. As part of the measures, the Civil Aviation Safety Authority will also publish a monthly report which will name airlines that have seriously breached safety regulations. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Communications giant Telstra is set to be partially privatised next year as two Independent Senators threw key support behind the Federal Government's plan to raise A$8 billion from the one-third sale. With a package of A$350 million for jobs and the environment for their respective States, Senators Mal Colston and Brian Harradine infiltrated the Opposition and minor parties by giving the sale the go-ahead. Page 1.

The fiancee of assassinated New South Wales MP John Newman, Lucy Wang, has sought an urgent meeting with the State Government and the NSW Police Commissioner, Peter Ryan, as investigators close in on her lover's killers. The meeting was requested by Wang after she became concerned that media reports of imminent arrests would harm police investigations. Page 1.

As the New South Wales Police Royal Commission continued yesterday, a police senior sergeant denied that he had covered-up the arrest of Justice David Yeldham in 1988. The police officer denied he had indicated to an arresting officer that Yeldham - who cmmitted suicide recently following allegations of paedophilia - was "on side" with the police and no further action should be taken against the Judge after he was arrested at Central railway station. Page 1.

The New South Wales Police Association has signalled it may shift all its members from State to Federal awards as part of a bid to secure an industrial right of appeal against the Police Commissioner's new sacking powers. The move would place a major hurdle before Commissioner Peter Ryan as he embarks on his goal to rid the force of corrupt police over the next few weeks. Page 2.
THE AGE

Support in the Senate was clinched yesterday for the Howard Government's A$8 billion partial privatisation of Telstra, with an extra A$350 million added into the deal. The extra money is expected to go to the States of Independent Senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston, in what the Opposition dismisses as "pork-barrelling". Page A1.

The Federal Government was told yesterday Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett received a A$400,000 defamation payout from Consolidated Press, a former part-owner of Crown Casino, at the time the State Government was increasing the size of the casino. A Victoran casino inquiry committee member, Senator Robert Ray, raised allegations the rumoured payout was part of widespread political corruption surrounding the awarding of the casino license. Page A1.

Repeated interjections by Victorian Opposition Leader John Brumby during a Question Time which focused on the Government's contentious auditor-general review, were punished by the Speaker who denied Labor its next question. This punishment resulted in a walkout by Labor MPs. Page A2.

According to data released by the Bureau of Tourism Research yesterday, visitors to Victoria are up 12 per cent to 2.9 million, maintaining the State's position as the second most popular state for interstate tourists. While New South Wales remains the top choice, Victoria has lifted its share of the market through an aggressive marketing campaign by Tourism Victoria. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
